tools.name: verify_email
tools.description: Check in real time whether an email address exists and can receive mail, by asking the recipient's mail server (no message is sent). Returns code "ok" (valid), "ko" (invalid) or "mb" (uncertain, such as a catch-all domain) with a message.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: verify_email · Private data: find_email · Public sink: verify_email, find_email · Destructive: find_email.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: verify_email · Private data: find_email · Public sink: verify_email, find_email · Destructive: find_email

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "find_email" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Find the work email address of a person from their name and their company domain.
